newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Children first victims in southern Vietnam floods.
newsitem.headline: Children first victims in southern Vietnam floods.

text.p: Nine children have been killed and thousands of people evacuated from homes in southern Vietnam amid the first serious flooding of the year in the Mekong River Delta, disaster officials said on Saturday.

A statement released by Hanoi's UN-sponsored, Disaster Management Unit said the worst affected areas were provinces bordering Cambodia, where all the casualties were reported and where more than 117,000 homes were flooded.
Roads in the area were submerged, adding to the problems facing relief efforts for the thousands of people who have had to leave their homes.

Officials at the International Federation of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies said waters in the area were continuing to rise, and the situation was therefore likely to worsen in the next few weeks.
"The peak has still not come. It's already worse than last year and approaching the levels seen in 1994," said the IFRC's Leif Tybell, who returned from the area on Friday.
In 1994, Mekong Delta flooding caused by monsoon rains cost the lives of some 400 people and caused damage worth $300 million.
Environmentalists say the annual problem is linked to deforestation in upstream areas and the erosion or diversion of natural water channels for farming.
Vietnam has already suffered serious storm and flood damage this year with around 400 people killed since July, mostly in poor northern areas of the country.
